statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-26130 (GHSA-4vgm-c2wm-63mw) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue: a crafted message to a SignalR server can exhaust an internal buffer. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, from 10.0.0 through 10.0.3 as affected and 10.0.4 as fixed (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-4vgm-c2wm-63mw, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/385, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.4/10.0.4.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries; 10.0.4-r0 is built from the v10.0.104 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.104), and its assemblies carry that tag's commit. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg and tar.gz archives: every build ships Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Core.dll from its own .NET release, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore10-runtime (all 87 Microsoft.AspNetCore assemblies there carry the build's version) and in the SDK, runtime packs and ASP.NET Core runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and as a reference assembly in aspnetcore10-targeting-pack and in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref nupkg of dotnet10-runtime-artifacts. 10.0.2-r0 and 10.0.3-r0 carry ASP.NET Core 10.0.2 and 10.0.3, which are affected; 10.0.4-r0 and every later build carry 10.0.4 or later, with Microsoft's fix. The range ends at 10.0.4-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-26130 (GHSA-4vgm-c2wm-63mw) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue: a crafted message to a SignalR server can exhaust an internal buffer. Microsoft lists the Linux ASP.NET Core runtime packs among the affected packages and fixed .NET 9 in 9.0.14 (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-4vgm-c2wm-63mw, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/385, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.14/9.0.14.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Core.dll ships in the ASP.NET Core shared framework in aspnetcore9-runtime, in the SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and in ASP.NET Core NuGet packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, and every implementation copy in a build carries that build's ASP.NET Core version. In 9.0.12-r0 and 9.0.13-r0 SignalR.Core is 9.0.12 and 9.0.13, which are affected; from 9.0.14-r0 on, the version is 9.0.14 or later, with Microsoft's fix. The range ends at 9.0.14-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
